mock_cpu_validation.scope: All harness orchestration Popen/run/group signals mocked. Synthetic model/media bytes are fixtures, not runtime evidence.

actual_owned_cpu_validation.scope: Actual owned ordinary CPU Python groups in Docker. No SDK, DDS, MuJoCo, Isaac, ONNX or GPU.
proofs: Actual direct group SIGTERM produces signed Popen returncode -15 and empty non-Z group.
Owned wrapper exits zero; previously observed child ignores TERM, survives bounded wait, receives group KILL, then non-Z group empty.
Different real group cannot be signalled through an old birth identity; it remains alive and is subsequently cleaned up only using its own captured identity.

superseded_history.reason: Independent validation proved PGID/SID number-only signaling could hit a reused leader or unknown-only orphan. Entire prior proposal files retained original bytes.

source_changes: Final worker nonzero gate after loop; no successful result unless direct rc0 and groups empty/ownership verified.
Independent session/group for each worker; initial leader pid/startticks must be actually read with matching PGID/SID.
Known member identities persist as pid/startticks. New members are absorbed only while at least one still-live known identity anchors exact group/session.
Reused leader birth, missing spawn birth, only unknown members, proc errors, or retired-group reappearance become sticky unknown; no signal is sent.
Observed empty group retires permanently; its numeric PGID/SID cannot be revived.
Polling refreshes group identities. First worker entry is observed with original entry SHA and native identity; it can differ from wrapper PID.
Historical group snapshots deep-copied to prevent later known-member absorption changing earlier events.
Cleanup waits direct worker and group; owned groups receive TERM then KILL with bounded wait. Unknown/live groups remain failures.
Diagnostic/stop-marker/log-close I/O errors are deferred until reaping/close attempts, then propagated.
Optional faulthandler env for a fresh cohort; inherited settings reported.

future_final_seal_requirements: Parent returncode 0 and both direct worker returncodes 0.
Final finally_wait_complete event: empty groups, ownership_verified true, ownership_state retired_empty, retired true, ownership_lost false, cleanup_errors empty, unreaped_roles empty.
Hash and bind both raw entries, parent raw receipt and current harness/plan/result identity; native entry pid/startticks must be a known member and its PGID/SID must match expected private group.

limits: No production/frozen-cohort source or old result was modified; patch does not repair historical missing worker statuses.
Actual process-group tests use only owned ordinary CPU Python children in Docker. SDK018, actual shell launchers, DDS, physics and GPU shutdown remain untested by this proposal.
A positive wrapper code does not identify its native child signal; actual self PID and fatal logs remain needed for attribution.
proc identity is within observer namespace; host PID/TID mapping is not inferred.
Unknown ownership is deliberately not signalled and may remain live/unreaped; report cannot claim cleanup succeeded.
Zombies are excluded from live membership; orphan reaping by system init is not verified.
Observation and signal are separate Linux operations; captured birth/continuous identity guards reduce reuse ambiguity but do not form a kernel-atomic process-group handle.
Do not run ignored candidate as simulator: ROOT is based on its temporary location. Reviewed application requires fresh plan/source/image/cohort and strengthened matrix sealing.
A result may have been written before final receipt/cleanup failure; nonzero parent exit must prevent successful sealing.
